item.title: MJR Morning Brief — October 30, 2026
item.description:
From Media Jobs Report, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
New research from Northwestern University's Medill Local News Initiative finds Americans increasingly skeptical of the news media ahead of the midterm elections. Only 32 percent have high confidence in accurate election reporting, while sharp partisan divisions persist over journalists' intentions. Local news outlets remain among the most trusted sources. Read more at Media Jobs Report.
Turning to radio,
Audacy’s 106.5 The Wolf in Kansas City is adding Mo and StyckMan to its weekday lineup. Their show will air from 3 to 7 p.m. Central Time starting November 2. The award-winning duo also hosts shows in Chattanooga, Richmond and Memphis, along with Audacy’s nationwide overnight program, “3rd Shift Country.”
In streaming news,
Peacock's new horror series Crystal Lake is off to a strong start. The Friday the 13th prequel generated 1.3 billion viewing minutes in its first 11 days, becoming Peacock's fourth-biggest scripted original debut. Starring Linda Cardellini, the eight-episode series is now streaming exclusively on Peacock.
On the education front,
The Missouri School of Journalism has named Amy Simons its next Associate Dean for Undergraduate Studies and Administration, effective May first. Simons, a professor and longtime faculty leader, succeeds Lynda Kraxberger, who is retiring after more than 35 years with the School. Simons will oversee undergraduate programs and student success initiatives.
In other media news,
On Air Fest is celebrating its 10th anniversary February 23rd through 25th in Brooklyn. The first-wave lineup includes Megan Rapinoe, Dr. Sanjay Gupta, Audie Cornish, Ari Shapiro and Dan Harris. The festival also features Bloomberg's Podcast Business Summit and the Ambies Awards, celebrating excellence in podcasting. Tickets are available now, with additional programming to be announced.
And finally,
SiriusXM is getting into the holiday spirit with 25 seasonal music channels beginning November second. The lineup includes Christmas classics, country, rock, jazz and soul, plus specialty channels featuring Jimmy Fallon, Hallmark, Smokey Robinson and Trans-Siberian Orchestra. Many channels will be available on the SiriusXM app and satellite radio throughout the holidays.
Find more media news, jobs, industry resources and free tools at MediaJobsReport.com.
